title: WPSS/1177/2019 of DUSHYANT KUMAR Vs UCO BANK

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1177 of 2019
Dushyant Kumar Ö Petitioner
Vs
UCO Bank & others Ö Respondents
Mr. B.D. Pande, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Honíble Manoj K. Tiwari, J. (Oral)
1. Petitioner is aggrieved by the order dated
17.05.2019 (Annexure No. 8 to the writ petition), whereby his
request for appointing defence representative in a disciplinary
proceeding pending against him, has been rejected.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that
petitioner was asked by the Enquiry Officer as to whether he
needs a defence representative in the pending inquiry against
him. Petitioner sought four days time to name the defence
representative and ultimately he nominated one Mr. S.K.
Saxena, who is a practicing Advocate in Kashipur, District
Udham Singh Nagar.
3. In the absence of any provision in the Service Rules
for appointment of an Advocate as a defence representative,
petitioner cannot claim assistance of an Advocate as defence
representative as of right. Accordingly, the said request of the
petitioner for appointing an Advocate as a defence
representative has been rightly turned down by the Enquiry
Officer.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that
petitioner is not insisting for assistance of an Advocate as his
defence representative and he may be permitted to nominate
some retired Bank employee as his defence representative.
5. Having regard to the nature of charges against the
petitioner and also the fact that petitioner is a Class-IV
employee, who is not much educated, therefore, the request
made by the petitioner deserves to be sympathetically
considered by the Competent Authority.

2
6. Accordingly, the writ petition is disposed of with
liberty to the petitioner to make a formal request for assistance
of a defence representative other than a Advocate to the
Competent Authority, within three days from today. If such
request is made, the Competent Authority shall examine the
same and take appropriate decision, in accordance with law,
within two weeks thereafter.
7. Let certified copy of this order be supplied to the
petitioner today itself on payment of usual charges.
 (Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
27.05.2019
Aswal
